questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted a place which i spoke the language was my big thing, so I only looked at english or scandinavian countries. And I wanted some places with cool natures, like huge trees, national parks, mountains ect. since I really enjoy hiking and camping. And I also chose Canada specifically cause i traveled there before and really enjoyed the people and country overall.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I was actually positively surprised by how helpful the university was, they were quick at answering, very helpful, send out a ton of information before, and had online seminars before with everything from helping with the ETA (Canadian visa) to getting to know the different clubs on the university. The only thing you were not sure to get help with was housing, but even then they really tried hard.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A lot of the same, there was a couple people assigned to help us and they were super sweet and helpful and always keen to talk and give recommendations also during the year, with making different activities. But the first days you had to find them, cause the orientations the first couple days was very aimed at first years, who are 17-18 years old... so makes you feel very much like the odd one out. But if you power through till friday, it starts monday. Then it is very helpful and so nice cause they have an entire day only for exchange students and here it was so helpful to make a big whats app group with everyone.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Airbnb is the safest way to go, overall, cause there is a lot of scammning on Facebook pages and so on. And if you are not staying an entire year don't count on getting on campus housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you go to Hamilton, DON'T STAY DOWN TOWN, it is sketchie and there is a lot of homeless persons. Either stay in Westdale or Dundas, which is also close to campus. Or find canadians to stay with a lot of them have houses and looking to rent out a room.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You have to do it yourselves, which sucks when you are in a new country where you don't know anyone, I would recommend talking to someone who already did the exchange at that university for advice.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I think it was pretty easy to get it assigned since you just need to write a letter. It is a bit harder with the exchange university mostly because they use other platforms.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I did not think the home university helped a lot. They were hard to get a hold of and came with half answers. But the exchange university was very helpful and you never felt like your questions were stupid so that was very nice.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got most of the classes I wanted, i got 3/4. I only had to take 4 courses, and since 2 of mine needed to partly elective, it was nice to get your first priorities. One course I didn't get I ended up spamming the faculty leader until I got a spot, for the leader I wouldn't recommened it but very effective still. Plus using the exchange card is helpful, cause you are seen as exotic when you are an exchange students, which is a nice card to pull.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be ready, some courses are very popular and are gonna be ripped away, so be fast and if you don't get a course try contacting the proffersor, cause they are usually very helpful. And do check the tutorial times, I found out to late that there was multiple to choose between so I just got the one suggested for me.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is easier to pass cause the grade is split up between multiple things but it also does require more work throughout the year.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Genreally the level is lower, which is nice if you are visiting for the country and culture cause leaves more time to travel. But the professors are better at teaching than back home so the lectures are really interesting and easy to follow. It is also easier to pass cause the grade is split up between multiple things but it also does require more work throughout the year.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I think it is a lot of the same. With lectures and tutorials, I had on course which was different but mostly the same. You can just feel the proffeseurs are more teaching aimed and not research aimed over there.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Principles of virologi 
Introductory Immunology
The Big Questions
Science of Fictional Characters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Principles of virologi - truly my favorite course, the proffesur, Doctor Mullarkey, is truly fantastic it is crazy.
Science of Fictional Characters  - this was a really fun course about how you use research, and trying to take risk in science in a different way, would highly recommed it. 
The Big Questions - fun course about astronomy, very easy to learn which is nice if you know nothing about it, but very much a fun course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You do go on trips and eat out a lot and the price for housing is typically more expensive another place.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: transport was less than expected which was nice. Buying food in grocery stores was more, which sucked.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: THE GYM WAS FREE, it was so nice and the gym was huge. You could also for pretty cheap prizes sign up for different training I did kick boxing. I know there was also other things like knitting club and the exchange commitee hosted a lot of events. But i mostly did a lot of training also joined the outdoor club for going on trips.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you like training, do that it is so accesible. And something that strengthen the exchange group and made my friend group was the boys made an intermural soccer team, and played games on sunday where everyone came out and rooted for them and after we went to get beer, this was really good for friendships.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Yes I recommened going on trips, but I would say wait and makes friends to go with you.
But go to Montreal and Quebec really nice city. When it is still warm I would also recommened going to Halifax a city on the east cost. Closer I would recommened national parks like Pennisula and Algonquin park which are so pretty. And of course going to the west coast to see Banff, Whistler, Vancouver. 
I know some people went to New York since it is close but due to Americas situation I personally didn't wanna go.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I would say okay easy, the people are way more polite and talkative like in the bus, supermarket and so on, which is very kind but coming from Denmark a big change from how the culture is here.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to them, they are sooooooooooo talkative, and actually want to talk so just start yapping with people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really, I think the culture is so mitch match because of the colonisation and because they are a generally a nice and open people it is really easy to adjust to the people.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The kindness, it makes it very easy to feel welcome in the country and that is super nice, cause they would just go up and talk to you and complient you which gives a good feeling.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be open minded and say yes, it makes it easier to get friends quicker when people remember you 
2. Travel around, save money up before so it is possible and not an issue, cause it is really a beautiful country which is worthwhile to visit.
3. Make friends with the other exchange group, even if it feels silly to go to another country to talk to people not from that country. But you are in the same boat as the other exchange students and the are generally more open and want to go out and explore than the canadians.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make a big exchange group quickly on whats app or a likewise app. And then just go to everything, even if you are a bit tired especially in the start, it really helps later cause you build up so many friendships and connections.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My friends i made, i mostly made exchange friends, but i got truly close with a lot of people which i cherish more than anything else i got on this exchange. And i actually enjoyed not knowing anyone before i left, cause i was forced in another way to make friends which was very nice.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Saying goodbye...
I think before you got there cause there is so many uncertainities both housing and with being in another country. But since i got there after the first week when you don't know anybody it is only great.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
